notes: Main disagreements, by frequency: (1) unit_stance on duty-type statements (verification, reporting, ask-first, existing-policy pointers): resolved to neutral when the statement does not take a position on whether AI may be used; (2) phase for institution-wide rules (general vs during-work or before-course or over-time): resolved to general when the passage is not tied to a course stage or a review step; (3) policy_type where one sentence touches two types (P24/P45/P36 for citation and plagiarism; P50/P77 for privacy compliance; P62/P52/P49 for research data and course materials; P02/P04/P87 for the welcoming default): resolved by the operative clause and the other type recorded in fit_note; (4) modality informs vs must for statements of responsibility (resolved by whether the passage assigns a duty); (5) document stance for the University guidelines (A delegates, B restrict): resolved to restrict because the document itself sets the ban-unless-permitted default for coursework. Unit boundaries: A merged the three rules of the 'Plagiarism rules apply' sentence and all four Act 848 items into single units; B split them. Resolved by splitting (one rule per unit), which adds the lobbying unit as a reconciler split. Of the 14 single-coder units, 12 were kept (6 A, 6 B) as real policy statements, including A's two citation/library-guide pointers, both recoded UNCOVERED; 2 were dropped (A's second Libraries citation sentence, merged with the preceding sentence as one rule; B's TIPS reporting unit, whose anchor pointed at the note-selling statement and not an AI statement). Final unit counts per document: [99, 13, 8] (the first includes one reconciler split, the lobbying unit).
